summary: Planning is now computed on your machine. The desktop app plans with the same shared engine as the web planner: object positions, twilight windows, the Sun and Moon, visibility percentages, clear windows and scores are calculated locally when you change the date or site, and preference changes (minimum altitude, Bortle class, moon-aware ranking, filters) update instantly without recalculating the night. Every displayed number is the same as before - behind the scenes the sky position is now precessed once per night instead of at every sample, a change far below anything shown. On slower or heavily throttled machines, changing the date or site with the full 12,000-object catalog enabled can take noticeably longer than in 0.6.17 (the app shows a busy indicator while it works); preference changes stay instant, and an asynchronous compute update is planned. Your local server remains as an automatic fallback, and the interface is unchanged.

Shared-core release. The desktop app and the web planner now compute every planning number with one shared engine, so the two can no longer drift apart. Three visible corrections come with it: object-type names and colours are identical in both apps (the desktop adopts the web palette); a grazing polar-night day can no longer report a sunrise without a sunset (Tromso in January showed a "sunrise" 29 minutes before its own sunset); and the night slider and the altitude chart now use the dark window whenever the sunset-to-sunrise pair is degenerate, instead of building an inverted range. Ordinary nights, DST transitions and southern-hemisphere nights are unchanged. Python still computes the desktop's planning payload.

Desktop patch release. The sky view is corrected: in "paint visible sky" mode the chart no longer draws a spurious centre ring or radial connector, never strokes the band outline, and hatches the area above the painted band instead of shading it as blocked. The same horizon legend now appears in the desktop and the web ("blocked by horizon" and "above band: open (assumed)"), and the web editor's profile preview hatches that assumed-open area too. This build also carries the immediately preceding sky-band fixes: painting the visible sky assumes the sky above the band is open unless you tick "block above band", and View full day is a real 24-hour toggle in both apps.

Editing and reliability release. The web panorama editor was rebuilt for precise work: a grouped two-row toolbar with the view controls on the image, gesture-level undo/redo, a confirmed and undoable Clear, a Revert, a clear saved/unsaved indicator, sharp HiDPI rendering, zoom and pan, denser alignment guides, and a live azimuth/altitude readout. Painting the visible sky now assumes the sky ABOVE your band is open (hatched with a legend entry) unless you tick "block above band", and holding the right mouse button erases continuously. The night scrub now spans sunset to sunrise by default, with a "View full day" option that restores a full 24 hours in BOTH apps - the desktop now has a real full-day grid too - and the minimum-altitude slider is longer in the top bar. The object list no longer has two entries sharing one id, web backups are truthful and roll back a failed restore, the desktop no longer dead-ends if you skip choosing a site, and only one panorama is active at a time.

Bug-fix and chart-tools release. On the all-sky chart the Sun and Moon could appear in the sky while they were really below the horizon - both apps now draw them only while they are actually up at the selected time. The web chart gains the desktop's magnitude slider (hide objects fainter than a chosen limit), the desktop chart's wheel-zoom now opens the same full rectangular window as the web, and the web panorama editor gains alignment guides (azimuth, altitude and horizon lines), joins a 360-degree panorama seamlessly at the edges, and fixes sky-mask "open above" handling and the compass labels on partial panoramas. Web cache tokens were bumped so the updated files reach returning visitors.

Consistency release: the desktop app and the web planner now agree everywhere. The night window is identical in both apps at every latitude - including polar twilight, where the web could pick the wrong night - the Dark time card shows the twilight level actually used for scoring, the minimum altitude follows the Bortle class immediately, and "Best targets tonight" only lists targets that really clear the sky during the night. Frame coverage and filter advice now read the same in both apps, and the arrow-key time step is 6/60 minutes in both.

Accuracy, safety and consistency release. Object positions were off by up to half a degree (a precession bug, fixed in all sky-calculation engines), importing a setup file can no longer read or write files outside your own archive, and the clear-window times no longer include twilight. The web planner now resolves the same night, moon and filter scores as the desktop in any time zone. This build also brings the desktop app up to date with every web change since 0.6.0.
Web: internal stylesheet version bump so the 0.6.7 layout reaches visitors who still had the old file cached.

The imaging-rig (framing) selector moved out of the menu and into the top bar, right next to the site selector - in both the desktop app and the web version. Web release; the desktop change arrives with 0.6.9.
Web: the Sites, Rigs and Targets forms no longer render before you open them.
Web: the last visible traces of the popularity score are gone (the "Popular" filter chip). The desktop's popularity sort option was removed in the same step and ships with 0.6.9.

Telescope presets are now a picker instead of automatic entries: a fresh setup starts empty and "Add rig" offers the Seestar / DWARF models or a custom rig. Web release; the desktop version arrives with 0.6.9.
Web: the community-popularity number is no longer displayed anywhere - it still breaks ties in the ranking, silently.
Web: fixed an update-order problem that could briefly serve the app's page before its scripts, leaving visitors with a broken view until they reloaded.
Web: sample telescope presets (ZWO Seestar, DwarfLab) with their field of view, plus layout fixes. They were added automatically at the time; 0.6.4 turned them into a picker.

AstroPilot is now NightSeam: new name, and the website has moved to nightseam.de. Planning and the image library work exactly as before. If you replace an older installation in place, rename data/astropilot.db to data/nightseam.db to keep your sites and captures.

Reliability release: a failed backup import can no longer wipe your data, planning now resolves the correct night at every location (timezone fix), safer panorama handling, and many small fixes in both apps.
Targets are ranked with community popularity as a silent tiebreaker, and moon-aware scoring now accounts for the Moon's phase, your filters and your sky brightness (Bortle class).
The web setup wizard is centred correctly, more controls carry proper accessibility labels, and the library and panorama handling got small fixes.
Better keyboard and screen-reader support (dialog roles, focus traps, labelled search), smoother handling of very large imports, and internal cleanups.
Safer backup import (a safety copy is written before anything is replaced), streamed uploads that no longer need the whole session in memory, and small web fixes.
The session journal was removed from both versions — planning and the image library are unchanged, but observed marks and journal notes are gone.
Horizon photos now survive reloading the page, and the “free space” layout setting works on any screen.
More stable time slider; changing the minimum altitude no longer flashes the target list.
Public release: open source (MIT), credits and notices, automatic update checker in the desktop app, download page.
Target grades (S–D) in the desktop app; weather with a 4-day forecast in both versions; new website.
Target grades (S–D) for the web; the sky map zoom now opens a wider rectangular view.
New interface: hamburger menu, Glass theme, desktop-style layout in the browser.
Web version: sites, rigs, custom targets and first-run setup.
The web version joined the project.
